statusNote: ⚠ NOT LIVE. The code is merged and builds, but torahsings.com DNS and the nginx vhost still point at the standalone app in W:/TorahSings.com. Until step 4 of tenants/README.md is done, this file describes what the process WOULD serve, not what a visitor gets.

brand.logoNote: Registry value, kept for schema agreement. The Torah Sings header does NOT render it — components/torahsings/layout/SiteHeader.tsx uses /zev-circle.png, because this tenant brings its own chrome rather than components/Header.tsx.
extraFonts: Spline Sans Mono — eyebrows, labels, note lines
Playfair Display — the Hebraic Christianity reading room
brand.themeVariant: data-accent='silver' is supported by the scoped sheet

tagline: The stars sang. The angels sang. Now you can hear it.
description: Torah Sings: there are songs hidden inside the Scriptures. Taken symbol by symbol, the Paleo-Hebrew text surfaces melodies that read as sung from the angelic perspective. Not canon, but something to consider.
audience: Seekers and students of the Hebraic roots of the faith. Three pathways — the sung Scriptures, the Hebraic Christianity reading room, and Learn Hebrew — on one membership.

seo.titleDefault: Torah Sings — The stars sang. The angels sang. Now you can hear it.
seo.canonicalNote: Derived from hosts[0], because NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is a single process-wide value and belongs to JubileePraise.

openGraph.description: The stars sang. The angels sang. Now you can hear it.

catalogue.sourceNote: 🔴 THE ONE TENANT THAT DOES NOT READ catalog-manifest.json. lib/tenants.ts carries a `catalog` field for exactly this: its albums come from app/web/content/torahsings/angels-catalog.ts, generated from the drive and grouped by canonical division rather than by artist.
catalogue.categoriesNote: 🔴 EMPTY, NOT NULL, and the difference is load-bearing. null means the whole shared catalogue; [] means none of it. A JubileePraise album is 404 here — verified 2026-08-17 against a production build, with no title or metadata in the response body.
catalogue.countsNote: No album or track totals here — README's rule, and it applies double to this tenant: the numbers live in the generated header of content/torahsings/angels-catalog.ts and change whenever that file is rebuilt.
catalogue.studioRootNote: The studio does not carry this tenant in its picker yet; studioMusicRoot is recorded as the parent of musicDrive so the shape matches the other tenants. There are no per-voice folders here — the tree is 66 book folders (01_Genesis … 66_Revelation), verified on the drive 2026-08-17.
catalogue.cdnPrefixNote: From the standalone repo's `images:deploy` script — rclone target jubilee-r2:jubileeverse-cdn/torahsings/. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDIA_BASE to the CDN prefix or audio falls back to /audio/placeholder-ambient.wav, a synthesized drone that is not music.
catalogue.manifestNote: Not in app/web/public/music/catalog-manifest.json at all, and deliberately so — reconciling 285 book-keyed albums into an artist-keyed manifest would mean inventing an artist for each. J:/torahsings.com/catalog-manifest.json is the standalone app's own separate file.
catalogue.generatedBy: scripts/build-angels-catalog.mjs, still only in W:/TorahSings.com — it has no counterpart in this repo yet, so regenerating means running it there and re-copying.
catalogue.scopeEnforcedAt: app/web/lib/manifest.ts load() for the shared catalogue (which yields nothing here), and app/page.tsx routing to TorahSingsHome via usesAngelsCatalog() before the truthiness check on categories

home.featuredNote: No pinned album. One rail per canonical division, in canon order.

navNote: Rendered by components/torahsings/layout/SiteHeader.tsx, which reads THIS list out of lib/tenants.ts rather than declaring its own. Literal labels where no translation exists yet; nav.playlists is translated like JubileePraise's.

routes.ownNote: /album/[id] is a path segment and does not collide with JubileePraise's query-based /album?c=CODE — both exist in the same build.
routes.sharedNote: JubileePraise's single implementation, served under this tenant's chrome. Torah Sings shipped its own forked copies of all eleven; they were deliberately NOT ported. Its 'Jubilee ID one door' sign-in is the one worth revisiting — as a change to JubileePraise's own /signin for every tenant, not as a duplicate.

chrome.shellNote: This tenant mounts its own header, footer, transport and intro modal instead of JubileePraise's. Exactly one shell mounts per request, branched in app/layout.tsx on usesAngelsCatalog(). Its catalogue rails and album detail drive AudioProvider directly, so mounting JubileePraise's FooterPlayer as well would give a visitor two transports fighting over one <audio>.
chrome.stylesNote: GENERATED from the standalone globals.css by W:/.claude-scratch/scope-css.mjs; every selector is scoped under [data-tenant='torahsings'], which layout.tsx stamps on <html>. Torah Sings names its primitives generically (.wrap .card .panel .pill .prose, bare h1/p/a, a :root token block) and would otherwise restyle the other three tenants.
chrome.session: Shared. lib/torahsings/jubilee-account.tsx reads JubileePraise's lib/auth tokens, so signing in on the shared /signin is visible here immediately. Torah Sings' own token keys were dropped for this reason.

membership.reconciledNote: ⚠ NOT reconciled with JubileePraise's own subscription system. /membership and /subscription are two separate pages and two separate price stories in one process. Open decision.
membership.freeTier: Tracks 1–2 of a gated album stream free; the album article and derivation tabs are always open.
membership.bookPrice: PLACEHOLDER — BOOK_PRICE_LABEL in lib/torahsings/format.ts was never set.

i18n.chromeTranslatedNote: Torah Sings' own chrome is English-only apart from the one nav item carrying an i18n key. The language picker lives in JubileePraise's Header, which this tenant does not mount.

production.nginxVhostNote: ⚠ DOES NOT EXIST YET. Nothing on the box answers for torahsings.com through this process. Create /etc/nginx/sites-available/torahsings.com proxying to 127.0.0.1:3030, matching the goPartyGiggles block.
production.originTlsNote: Not configured. Follow the goPartyGiggles pattern (port 80 only, Cloudflare terminating at the edge) unless an origin certificate is wanted.

api.note: The standalone app pointed at api.torahsings.com via its own next.config rewrite. Inside this process there is one API base and it is JubileePraise's.

runtime.devNote: localhost resolves to JubileePraise, not here. To see this tenant locally, send the Host header or add a hosts-file entry.

env.shared: all NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars are process-wide; there is no per-tenant env
env.needed: NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDIA_BASE for real audio; INTRO_VIDEO_URL for the intro film (the modal says 'film pending' without it)

deploy.note: One pm2 process serves all four hosts, so a deploy ships them together. This site cannot be shipped on its own.
deploy.gateNote: That gate reads catalog-manifest.json, which this tenant is not in. It neither validates nor blocks Torah Sings content.

studio.pickerNote: Not in the WPF studio's Website picker. Its catalogue is not manifest-backed, so the picker has nothing to enumerate.

origin.standaloneNote: Still present, still deployable, NOT deleted. It remains the live site until DNS moves.
origin.backup: W:/Backups/TorahSings.com-2026-08-17 — 1,280 files / 214.1 MB, verified against source
origin.framework: Standalone was Next 16 / React 19; ported down to this app's Next 14 / React 18. Only the async params/searchParams pattern needed changing (8 files, 4 of them in the ported set) — no React 19 APIs, no server actions, no use() hook.

notes: The three open decisions from the standalone README came across unresolved: the Prong II name ('Hebraic Christianity' is a working title), the standalone book price, and whether the free tier is songs 1–2 or first-song-only.
content/torahsings/angels-catalog.ts, hebraic-articles.ts and learn-hebrew-articles.ts are GENERATED (about 62,000 lines between them). Hand edits will be overwritten by the next regeneration.

The derivation engine (lib/torahsings/derivation.ts) has a verification script in the standalone repo that recomputes every album's note line from scratch and fails the build on drift. That script was NOT ported; nothing in this repo currently guards it.
